name: Blue Grass
lede: Blue Grass is a very dark green in the Maerz and Paul color dictionary, and its name points at a plant it hardly resembles.

sections.title: A name with no color entry
sections.body:
The color books consulted give no definition of this color. Paterson's dictionary has entries only for the music, *bluegrass*, and for Kentucky's nickname, the Bluegrass State [1][4]. Neither describes a color, and the grass itself is green rather than blue, and the books consulted do not explain the name.

One psychology text mentions grass only as the example of a thing a color-blind person has learned to call green [5]. That is not a color of this name either, and it should not be read as one.

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is #19382F, a dark green with a low chroma, close to the library's nearest named neighbor, Bottle Green [3]. A screen shows it only approximately [3]. Compare [[green]] and [[viridian]] for greens that do have documented histories [3]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 21, chroma 14 and hue 172 degrees [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this dark green in 117 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [2]. Paul Cezanne is the painter who holds it most often, in 4 paintings [2]. Measured values are screen approximations of varnished canvases [2].

questions.q: In Paterson's dictionary, what does 'bluegrass' name?
True or false: the books consulted define Blue Grass as a color.

openers: The name says blue; the swatch is a very dark green.
